rv.q: This venture has strong narrative from Ker and Reed with light grace notes from British musical theatre's most profitable pair.
It's not a bad show, but it's an odd fit for a main house Christmas production, and taking the piss out of Christmas feels perversely un-Christmassy.
Unfortunately, while separate pieces of the show work, they struggle to come together into a truly cohesive piece.
Overall, Sherlock Holmes and the 12 Days of Christmas is a triumphant, festive treat; it's witty, suspenseful and unapologetically theatrical.
A real Christmas cracker of a show, if you're looking for a great gift for your nearest and dearest this festive season... why not go for two tickets to this instead?
A strong script and sharp comedy performances make this a fun festive night out as you count down to the big day.
Uneven pacing and a largely forgettable score prevent the show from reaching its full potential.
It is amusing rather than laugh-out-loud funny, heartfelt yet rambling, spirited but lacking a clear narrative drive.

Sherlock Holmes and The 12 Days of Christmas is a joyful sleigh-ride of a show—clever enough for Holmes aficionados, warm and witty enough for families, and bursting with enough Christmas cheer to thaw even the iciest of villains.
